evidence.quote: The Sentry web API is used to access the Sentry platform programmatically.
Authentication tokens are passed using an auth header, and are used to authenticate as a user or organization account with the API.
A Sentry user can belong to multiple organizations. The access token only provides access to the specific organization the user selected during the OAuth flow.
API Keys: A deprecated authentication method using HTTP Basic Auth, though still supported for existing accounts.

result.notes: Sentry's REST API ("web API") is large (organizations, projects, issues, events, alerts, releases, etc.). Auth: organization/personal auth tokens (bearer), OAuth2 apps (authorization code + PKCE + device flow), and a deprecated Basic-Auth API-key method still honored for legacy accounts. Free "Developer" plan explicitly excludes the "API & third-party integrations" feature per the pricing comparison table — API access requires the paid Team tier (which has a free trial), hence self_serve_trial rather than self_serve_free. Creating an auth token additionally requires an org Manager/Admin role. Sentry publishes an official MCP server (getsentry/sentry-mcp, 854★) reachable via mcp.sentry.dev, also listed as a feature of the free plan (chat/agent access to Sentry data), distinct from the paid REST API gate.
result.one_liner: Sentry is an error-monitoring/observability platform with a large REST API for managing projects, issues, events, and alerts programmatically.
